claims.quote: If a consumer calls `cancel()` and also commits the value to state (for example an app-level handler that always stores the value), the field still clears errors, validates and updates dirty and filled.
claims.notes: Related to CL-r-cancel-controlled, graded on its own words. True: the controlled branch returns before the isCanceled check and useValueChanged never reads it. The change announces 'details.cancel() in onValueChange now stops the internal handling'. Under Delivery rule 3 the application both canceled and stored the value; the stored value governs and the field follows it, so the promised outcome arrives and the cancel wording is untrue in this case: minor defect, matching the saved ruling on the related claim (first-round 21).
evidence: clone/packages/react/src/field/control/FieldControl.tsx: `if (isControlled) { return; }` precedes the isCanceled check; useValueChanged block calls clearErrors, setDirty, setFilled, validation.change.
packet.md PR body: 'details.cancel() in onValueChange now stops the internal handling.'
